VERIFICATION AND TWO ADDITIONAL COORDINATES, recorded ON THIS BEAD rather than left in the
coordination topic, because a finding in a 2000-post board is a sentence and a finding on the bead
is an artifact. Whoever takes this should not have to re-measure any of it.

THE FOUR CLAIMS IN THE BODY, CHECKED LINE BY LINE IN candidates.scala:

  :10   final case class Nomination(ref, channel: String, rank: Int, rawScore: Option[Double],
                                    space: Option[String], receipt: Option[String])
        channel, space and receipt are raw strings. CONFIRMED.
  :131  Nomination(r, channel, i, Some(d), space, Some(s"level:$level"))
        the semantic generator's receipt IS a hierarchy label. CONFIRMED verbatim.
  :147  Nomination(r, Channels.lexical, i, None, None, None)
        lexical nominations carry no receipt. CONFIRMED.
  :27   lazy val ranked = nominations.map(_.ref).distinct.sorted
        `distinct` is the exact line where nomination provenance is discarded; the aligner consumes
        `ranked`. CONFIRMED - one line, which is why it was easy to miss.

COORDINATE 1: THE RAW SCORE ALREADY DECIDES MEMBERSHIP, NOT ONLY ORDER.

  :124  val scored = nodes.flatMap(n => semantic(unit, n).toOption.map(d => (n.ref, d)))
  :127  .sortBy { case (r, d) => (d, r.key) }
  :128  .take(perLevel)

The sort feeds a take, so `d` determines WHICH nodes become nominations at all. Nothing between
:124 and :131 requires `d` to be finite. A finiteness requirement therefore belongs at :124, BEFORE
the sort - not as a validation on the published record.

MEASURED, rather than reasoned about (I ran the same shape in a scratch suite):

  Ordering[Double] in scope   scala.math.Ordering$DeprecatedDoubleOrdering$
  compare(NaN, 1.0)           1        NaN sorts GREATER than every real number
  compare(NaN, NaN)           0        so it IS a total order
  sortBy on (0.5, NaN, 0.1)   0.1, 0.5, NaN

So ordering is deterministic today - BUT BY INHERITANCE FROM A DEPRECATED IMPLICIT, not by
declaration. Scala 2.13 split TotalOrdering from IeeeOrdering precisely because the choice matters.
If the deprecation is enforced, or anyone imports IeeeOrdering locally, ordering becomes non-total
and this code changes behaviour with NO DIFF AT THE CALL SITE. "Explicit deterministic ordering"
therefore means writing the ordering down, not observing that it currently works.

TWO FAILURE MODES BELOW THAT, and which one you get is data-dependent:
  - scored.size >  perLevel : the NaN entry sorts last and is DROPPED by the take. The node silently
                              stops being a candidate. Not detected, not recorded, not reported.
  - scored.size <= perLevel : the NaN entry SURVIVES and Some(NaN) enters Nomination.rawScore and
                              the published record.

COORDINATE 2: THIS BEAD TURNS Nomination INTO A RECEIPT, AND IT IS A PUBLIC CASE CLASS.

  :10  final case class Nomination(...)

Today it is a hint, so forgeability is uninteresting. The moment it carries provider identity,
geometry identity and a derivation receipt, `Mirror.fromProduct` mints one from any package with any
provenance the caller likes - an audit record attesting a derivation that never ran. That is the
same defect sealed four times in this module already (StructuralReductionReceipt and siblings,
bd-01M17ZNXY6). The construction boundary is PART of this design, not a follow-up to it.

ONE OBSERVATION ON WHY :131 HAPPENED, worth keeping because it argues for the stratum/receipt split
rather than merely asserting it: someone put the hierarchy stratum in the receipt field because
there WAS a field and no rule about what belonged in it. A typed `stratum` and a typed `receipt`
cannot be confused that way.

I have changed no code. Recorded by claude-storymodel4s-m1; align is my module and I will take this
if the chief assigns it, but the measurements stand whoever does.
